messages:
mike: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a lightweight compatibility layer that sits at the front of runtime nodes to translate requests between Hosted/Dedicated/Private shapes. The goal: single routing + minimal per-mode branching inside runtime. POC in my branch, ping me for link.

elaine: curious — how much latency are we adding? :thinking_face:

mike: Measured ~1.8ms p50 in the POC for header translation and small auth checks. Main cost is extra hop when doing KMS sign-through for private customers.

sujan: Concerned about semantics drifting. If we translate call shapes, how do we preserve observability (trace ids, tenant ids) and sampling? We can't lose token-level billing attribution.

katie: Maybe we keep a minimal invariant: passthrough for tracing headers (x-request-id, traceparent), canonical tenant header (x-rd-tenant), and attach a translation header with original-mode metadata. Example:
```http
X-RD-Tenant: tenant_42
X-RD-Original-Mode: hosted
traceparent: 00-...-00
```

mike: Exactly. Also propose schema v1 for translation header so we can evolve. We add fallthrough: if translation fails, route to the same-mode runtime (no automatic cross-mode fallback). Avoids surprise QoS changes.

elaine: What about auth? Private wants customer KMS and signed tokens. Do we accept tokens signed by external KMS?

sujan: We should validate tokens at the edge when possible. For private, edge verifies signature with customer's cert; for hosted we use internal token service. Translation layer CAN exchange token types but must not keep plaintext keys.

katie: Ops note: we need audit logs for any token exchange. Put audit events into control-plane audit sink w/ masked material.

mike: Implementation options: a) sidecar proxy per runtime node (fast, local) b) centralized translator service (easier ops, single point) c) library embedded in runtime (lowest hop but couples runtimes). Tradeoffs:
- sidecar: good perf, per-node config complexity
- centralized: simpler rollout, higher tail latency and SLO concerns
- library: fastest but tight coupling and increases release surface

elaine: My +1 for sidecar; we already do sidecars for metrics. But we need consistent config distribution.

sujan: If sidecar, need health-check semantics: translator must expose /ready and a blackhole policy so runtime can bypass if translator unhealthy. Also circuit-breaker.

katie: Rollout plan suggestion: canary on staging -> small subset of Dedicated -> Private opt-in -> global switch for Hosted. Use feature flag for translation enabled per-tenant.

deploy-bot: deploy starting: canary group 'translation-proxy' -> deployed to infra/staging at 20231105T21:44Z

mike: Next steps: I'll open an RFC with interface sketch and a prototype benchmark. Action items: mike -> RFC + perf numbers, sujan -> threat model for auth exchange, elaine -> config distrib and k8s helm changes, katie -> audit + telemetry mapping. Any other objections?

sujan: no objections from security side but will review threat model asap.

elaine: +1

katie: +1

mike: Thanks — will post link to RFC once ready. :rocket:
